cognate: Gk λείπω = Lat. (re)linquo (*leykʷ-); Gk ὀστέα = Lat. ossa (*h₃esth₁-), both neuter acc. pl.
drift_or_renewal: subject renewed: Homeric θυμός vs Lucretius' vital heat/air (calor, aer: the anima-substance); Latin adds re- and pairs ossa with venas
shared_syntax: verb 'leave' + acc. pl. 'bones', subject = the life-principle leaving the body
context: the moment of death described as the vital principle abandoning the bones; Homer's formula is a fixed verse-end (6x in the Homer corpus); Lucretius 3.123 describes the escape of vital heat and air at death
phrase: λίπε δ̓ ὀστέα θυμός ~ ossa relinquit
note: Lucretius knew Homer and Ennius well, so this may be literary imitation, not inheritance; the single Latin attestation and the natural imagery keep confidence low. No Indic match found (asthi + ric/hā/tyaj/muc absent in RV/AV/epic DCS); GLAUx Greek outside Homer has none either.

near_miss.why_not: Irish 'gilithir snechta' is a generic colour simile of a stock beauty description; Serbian 'снијежне јабуке' (snowy apples = breasts) is a different figure; apple in the Irish context is a measure of apples on heads; no shared collocation.
OIr. míl ~ Gk μῆλον is a good cognate, but Irish lists hound, beast and deer as hunter/prey, Homer has dogs guarding sheep; contexts not congruent, co-occurrence generic.

near_miss.lead: flaith / fáith ~ valda / Óðinn; fír flatha
near_miss.why_not: Only shared roots; 'fír flatha' (ruler's truth) is a known Irish theme but the Edda partner 'einn veldr Óðinn' is not a parallel to it.

near_miss.lead: ba ríg, ba fáid, ba fili (king, seer, poet)
near_miss.why_not: Völuspá stanza on Baldr shares nothing beyond the Óðinn/fáith root; no phrase.

near_miss.lead: tears wetting the breast (déra ... co mbo fliuch ... bruinne)
near_miss.why_not: An Acallam stock phrase; Lucretian partners are physics of liquids, no mourning context; any cross-branch parallel (e.g. Homeric tears wetting the chest) is not in the slab and the image is natural.

near_miss.lead: knee + ground in a feat of strength
near_miss.why_not: glún/jānu and talam/tala co-occur generically; no shared figure.

near_miss.lead: worm in the head as cause of disease (cruimh ... 'na chinn ~ krimi ... śīrṣaṇya)
near_miss.why_not: OIr. cruim = Skt. kṛmi exact, but the head words are not cognate, the Irish is a narrative death in a late prose text, the Vedic a worm charm (and śīrṣaṇya is in the context line); worm-disease belief is widespread, so chance cannot be excluded.
In the Irish, rúad qualifies the ráith (fort), not the apples (which are golden/purple-headed); 'red apple' in ON and Serbian is generic.
Irish 'pledged with an oath' vs ON 'repay deceit with lie': different meaning (oath vs lie) and relation; root co-occurrence only.
Irish 'father hid from son, mother from daughter' (secret) vs Euripides' incest list; kin pairs are generic; the genealogies are formulaic only within ON prose.
Deer words not cognate; 'red' for red deer is a natural species description; the Vedic is a potency charm simile, the Irish a hunt list.

near_miss.lead: breakdown of kin bonds in evil years (son will not give a morsel to father, daughter to mother, friend to friend)
near_miss.why_not: Strong motif (cf. Hesiod Op. 182ff., Völuspá 45) but those are not in the slab; the slab partners (Lucretius' plague, AV sin of mother/father) do not share it; and the Irish (seven years of plenty and seven of famine) is modelled on Genesis 41 with Christian apocalyptic colouring (cf. Mark 13:12).

near_miss.lead: burial sequence: stone raised over grave, funeral games held, name written in ogham
near_miss.why_not: An attractive parallel to Homeric burial (tomb, stele, games), but no Homeric burial passage is in the slab; Herodotus' 'wrote down the name' of farm owners is unrelated; scríbaid is a Latin loan.

error.correct_reading: copula: 'gur bhó' = co ro bo 'so that ... was' (wet)
error.evidence: the phrase 'cor' bo fliuch' recurs in G303000 #1:1025 in the same sentence frame

error.correct_reading: as(s)na = prep. a(s) + plural article na: 'iar (fothrucud) asna losaib-sin', 'after bathing in/from those herbs'
error.evidence: followed by 'losaib' dat. pl. of lus 'herb'; no rib in the context

error.correct_reading: ós 'over' (prep.): 'ós a chind' over his head (grave)
error.evidence: parallel 'ro tócbad a lia oss a lighi' (#1:926), stone raised over his grave

error.correct_reading: feraid 'pours, provides', here passive 'ro ferad cluiche' funeral games were held; not the root of Gk ὁράω
